subject: humanities
passage: When the pianist Delia Moreau released her first solo album, few critics knew what to make of it. Its pieces were long and slow, built from simple melodies that returned again and again with small changes. One reviewer complained that the record "never quite arrives anywhere." Another, writing in a small jazz magazine, argued that the refusal to arrive was the point, comparing the experience of listening to the album to ______ light move across a wall." Neither critic, it turned out, had predicted how widely the album would come to be loved.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The quoted words "watching light move across a wall" are the object of the preposition "to." When a quotation is woven into a sentence this way, it takes no introductory punctuation; like the earlier quotation after "that," it simply continues the sentence.
explanation.A: Correct. No punctuation separates the preposition "to" from the quotation that serves as its object.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma can't separate the preposition "to" from its object, even when the object is a quotation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, and it can't come between a preposition and its object.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, and the quotation is not one.
